record_type: Historical source identity, reading observations and bounded retrieval coverage

principal_corrections: The DCA evaluation panel concluded on 25 February 1982 and the Director of DCA approved the following day, before the Task Force's March recommendation. Not recorded here.
The Task Force's grounds are six, not three.
'to produce essentially proposals' is a misquotation of 'to prepare what were essentially proposals', and it is on printed p. 7, not pp. 7-8.
The 'no really convincing set of comparative costs' sentence concerns common user networks against dedicated links, not the two designs.
A normalized comparative cost analysis existed and 'gave a heavy edge to REPLICA'.
The bounded protocol-keyword negative holds for TCP, IP, Transmission Control Protocol and Internet Protocol, but 'Internet' occurs once at printed p. 3 and 'protocols' once at printed p. 39.
The DSB epilogue is legible and was read in full; the degraded-scan limitation recorded here does not hold for the verified copy.
DCEC-TN-8-83 covers the design process only through January 1982, and its shared traffic model computed TCP overhead for both designs.

sources_examined.identity: R. Prishivalko, Modeling Efforts for the AUTODIN II 'Fly-Off' Study, DCEC Systems Analysis Division R820, DCEC-TN-8-83, August 1983
sources_examined.prior_state: Not previously recorded in this project.
sources_examined.why_it_matters: DCEC supported both design teams and the evaluation team, so this is the closest examined account to the missing evaluation record. It independently dates the tasking to September 1981, names the DIN II and Replica teams, describes the shared URDB requirements baseline and its defects, lists the shared models (GUPTA, CULINES, MUXLOC/CONLOC, GRINDER), and states that performance criteria were never specified sufficiently to permit meaningful comparison of the two designs.
